title: Drawing and Painting Expressive Little Faces: Step-by-Step Techniques for Creating People
description: In Drawing and Painting Expressive Little Faces , artist and popular Skillshare instructor Amarilys Henderson shares her practical and creative techniques for drawing and painting faces with style and personality. title: Draw It in Stages: 30 Progressive Lessons for Adults Who Think They Can't Draw — How to Dr
description: You weren't missing talent. The teaching was missing a step. Ever wondered what happened between one step and the next? Ever quit a drawing book because it moved too fast? Ever thought, Maybe I just can't draw ? The problem usually starts in the middle. Most beginner books show you where to start and what the finished picture should look like. Then, somewhere along the way, the instructions make a leap. That's where beginners get stuck. Every drawing here is broken into six or eight progressive steps . Nothing suddenly appears, nothing important is skipped, and each stage keeps what came before and adds one manageable change. Instead of wondering how did they get from that to this? , you always know what to do next. 30 progressive lessons. More than 200 illustrated steps. Four full pages per lesson, six for the fifteen more advanced ones, in a large 8.5 x 11-inch format. Inside, you'll learn to: Build control before complexity — lines, curves, circles and simple forms, until the pencil goes where you send it. Turn basic shapes into real objects — an apple, a cup, a chair, a ball, a glass, a spoon. Understand light and shading — how a few values make a flat shape feel solid, without getting buried in theory. Draw plants and animals — leaves, flowers, trees, cats, dogs and birds, by the same gradual approach. Create depth in a landscape — how foreground, middle ground and background make space. Approach faces without guesswork — an eye, a nose, a mouth, a whole face, then hands and the figure. Combine it into complete scenes — the later lessons bring earlier skills together instead of introducing something new. Recover when a drawing goes wrong — every lesson has a Wrong turn box: the common mistake, and the move that fixes it, so one crooked line doesn't end the evening.
